checklist.name: Financial Comprehensiveness
checklist.criteria_description: Evaluates how thoroughly the response covers all required financial indicators, comparative analyses, and anomalies with appropriate depth and technical accuracy.
checklist.1-2: Critical financial indicators are missing or grossly inaccurate. No meaningful year-over-year comparisons. Financial terms are used incorrectly or inconsistently. Contains serious technical errors.
checklist.3-4: Covers only basic financial indicators with limited depth. Year-over-year comparisons are superficial. Several key financial metrics (like debt-to-equity ratio or cash flow analysis) are missing or poorly explained.
checklist.5-6: Includes most required financial indicators with adequate explanations. Year-over-year comparisons are present but lack detailed analysis. Some financial anomalies are identified but not thoroughly analyzed.
checklist.7-8: Comprehensive coverage of all required financial indicators with detailed explanations. Thorough year-over-year comparisons with meaningful insights. Financial anomalies are well-identified with clear implications.
checklist.9-10: Exceptional coverage of all financial indicators with expert-level explanations and nuanced interpretations. Year-over-year comparisons include sophisticated trend analysis. Financial anomalies are identified with insightful root cause analysis and strategic implications.

checklist.name: Business Unit Analysis Quality
checklist.criteria_description: Assesses the depth, clarity, and strategic value of the business unit performance analysis, including comparative metrics and contextual insights.
checklist.1-2: Business unit analysis is absent or extremely superficial. No meaningful performance metrics or comparisons between units. Analysis lacks any strategic context or actionable insights.
checklist.3-4: Limited analysis of only some business units. Performance metrics are basic with minimal comparative analysis. Little connection between business unit performance and overall company strategy.
checklist.5-6: All major business units are covered with basic performance metrics. Some comparative analysis between units is provided. Connections to company strategy are present but not fully developed.
checklist.7-8: Detailed analysis of all business units with comprehensive performance metrics. Strong comparative analysis highlighting strengths and weaknesses. Clear connections between unit performance and strategic objectives.
checklist.9-10: Exceptional analysis of all business units with sophisticated performance metrics and benchmarking. Comparative analysis reveals critical interdependencies between units. Insights directly inform strategic decision-making with clear action paths for improvement.

checklist.name: Risk and Opportunity Assessment
checklist.criteria_description: Evaluates the quality of risk identification, market change analysis, competitive landscape assessment, and future opportunity evaluation.
checklist.1-2: Risks and opportunities are either completely overlooked or mentioned without any meaningful analysis. No market trends or competitive factors are identified. Future development considerations are absent.
checklist.3-4: Basic risks are identified but lack depth. Market changes are mentioned superficially. Competitive landscape is incomplete or oversimplified. Limited future opportunities are presented without strategic context.
checklist.5-6: Key risks and opportunities are identified with adequate analysis. Market changes are described with some supporting evidence. Competitive landscape covers major factors. Future development opportunities have reasonable strategic context.
checklist.7-8: Comprehensive risk analysis with prioritization and potential impacts. Market changes are analyzed with relevant data points. Competitive landscape is thorough and insightful. Future opportunities are well-connected to strategic objectives.
checklist.9-10: Exceptional risk analysis with sophisticated probability and impact assessments. Market changes are analyzed with forward-looking indicators. Competitive landscape reveals strategic vulnerabilities and advantages. Future opportunities are presented with innovative strategic pathways and implementation considerations.

checklist.name: Visual Presentation and Data Visualization
checklist.criteria_description: Assesses the effectiveness, clarity, and sophistication of tables, charts, and visual elements used to present financial data and support decision-making.
checklist.1-2: Visual elements are missing or extremely poorly designed. Tables and charts are confusing, inaccurate, or inappropriate for the data presented. No explanatory notes accompany visual elements.
checklist.3-4: Basic tables and charts are present but poorly designed or difficult to interpret. Visual elements add little value to understanding the data. Explanatory notes are minimal or unclear.
checklist.5-6: Adequate tables and charts that correctly present key data. Visual elements support understanding but may lack sophistication. Explanatory notes provide basic context for visual elements.
checklist.7-8: Well-designed tables and charts that effectively communicate financial data. Visual elements enhance understanding with appropriate formats for different data types. Clear explanatory notes that highlight key insights.
checklist.9-10: Exceptional data visualization with sophisticated, intuitive, and highly effective tables and charts. Visual elements transform complex data into immediately actionable insights. Explanatory notes expertly guide interpretation and decision-making based on the visualized data.

checklist.name: Report Structure and Format Adherence
checklist.criteria_description: Evaluates how well the response follows the requested management report structure, formatting requirements, and overall organization for executive decision-making.
checklist.1-2: Format completely ignores specified requirements. No discernible structure aligned with management report standards. Missing essential components like cover title or table of contents. Extremely difficult for executives to navigate.
checklist.3-4: Basic structure present but significant deviations from requested format. Some components missing or poorly executed. Organization is inconsistent, making executive review challenging. Limited adherence to the provided reference format.
checklist.5-6: Follows most formatting requirements with reasonable structure. Contains required components like cover, table of contents, and overview. Organization is logical but could be more intuitive for executive decision-making.
checklist.7-8: Well-structured report following all specified format requirements. Clear organization with effective use of sections, bullet points, and formatting consistent with reference materials. Designed with executive decision-making in mind.
checklist.9-10: Exceptionally structured report that perfectly adheres to all format requirements while enhancing readability and decision support. Sophisticated use of formatting elements that guide attention to critical information. Organization optimized for rapid executive assessment and decision-making.

outline:
[Paragraph 1 - Main Point : 【press release：Based on the uploaded financial market data, write...】 - 【第1章：Headline】 - Craft a data-driven headline that explicitly states Xiaomi Group achieved record net profit in 2018 after three years of financial restructuring (2015–2018), highlighting the turnaround from prior losses and naming at least one catalyst—such as the Mi MIX series launch or IoT ecosystem expansion. Between 2015 and 2018, Xiaomi executed a comprehensive transformation that converted financial vulnerability into sustainable profitability and investor confidence. Starting from a $300 million operating cash flow deficit and negative net margins, the company achieved a $2.5 billion net profit by 2018, with net profit margin expanding from -2% to 5.1% and return on invested capital (ROIC) rising to 12%. This performance was underpinned by bold strategic shifts and rigorous operational discipline. The 2017 launch of the Mi 6 catalyzed a premium smartphone strategy, lifting average selling prices by 35%, while the IoT ecosystem grew at an 80% compound annual rate to generate $7 billion in revenue by 2018. Operationally, receivables turnover improved from 78 to 42 days, inventory turnover rose from 4.2x to 6.1x, and the current ratio strengthened from 0.9 to 1.4, enabling a surge in operating cash flow to $3.4 billion. Balance sheet resilience followed, with debt-to-equity halving from 1.2 to 0.4—further bolstered by the post-IPO conversion of $1.8 billion in redeemable preferred stock. Supported by 7,584 patents filed by year-end 2018, Xiaomi’s hardware-software integration fueled a self-reinforcing cycle: higher-margin products enhanced liquidity, which accelerated R&D, ecosystem expansion, and efficiency gains, ultimately redefining its global competitiveness through innovation-driven financial strength. - Word Count : 416]
[Paragraph 2 - Main Point : 【press release：Based on the uploaded financial market data, write...】 - 【第2章：Subheadline Development Aligned with Strategic Framing】 - Write a subheadline under 20 words that directly links Xiaomi’s 2015–2018 profit recovery to one concrete strategic outcome: either (a) gross margin expansion from premium smartphone launches, (b) stabilized operating cash flow through receivables management, (c) reduced preferred stock liabilities post-redemption, or (d) improved inventory turnover enabling leaner operations. Use active verbs and financial terminology appropriate for institutional investors. Between 2015 and 2018, Xiaomi executed a comprehensive transformation that fused operational rigor with an ecosystem-driven strategy to rebuild financial health and unlock scalable profitability. Operationally, the company reversed negative operating cash flow of –RMB 2.2 billion in 2016 to +RMB 12.3 billion in 2017 by tightening channel inventory, reducing receivables days from 60 to 38 through distributor prepayment terms, and accelerating inventory turnover from 4.2x to 6.1x. These measures shortened the cash conversion cycle by 25 days, lifted the current ratio to 1.3x, and extinguished $1.4 billion in redeemable preferred shares at its 2018 IPO—resolving structural liquidity concerns. Concurrently, Xiaomi leveraged its 'triathlon' model of smartphones, IoT, and internet services: strategic launches like the Mi Mix raised smartphone ASPs by 22%, while IoT scaled to over 100 million connected devices, fueling internet services revenue to triple from RMB 3.2 billion (2015) to RMB 9.6 billion, with 60% margins. This diversification expanded gross margin from 3.6% in 2016 to 12.7% in 2018—not via pricing but through centralized procurement and lean manufacturing. Investor metrics reflected this shift: ROE swung from –15.2% (2015) to +12.4% (2018), free cash flow turned positive in 2017 and reached RMB 9.8 billion in 2018 (8.1% of revenue)—outpacing peers like Samsung (6.5%)—and capex prioritized high-ROI segments, such as IoT R&D (up 40%, yielding 35% segment margin). With 7,584 granted patents, Xiaomi also positioned itself for future IP licensing revenue, demonstrating capital efficiency beyond low-margin hardware. - Word Count : 347]
[Paragraph 3 - Main Point : 【press release：Based on the uploaded financial market data, write...】 - 【第3章：Lead Paragraph: Synthesizing Strategic Turnaround and Financial Milestones】 - Compose a 60–80 word lead paragraph opening with Xiaomi’s 2018 net profit figure (RMB 13.5 billion, per IPO prospectus), then immediately connect it to three specific drivers: (1) the 2016–2017 Mi MIX and Mi 6 launches that lifted smartphone ASP by 18%, (2) reduction in days sales outstanding from 72 to 49 between 2015–2017, and (3) growth of its IoT segment to 25% of revenue by 2018, supported by its portfolio of 7,584 patents as of 2018. Between 2015 and 2018, Xiaomi executed a transformative strategy that simultaneously resolved liquidity concerns and built sustainable profitability through integrated innovation and operational rigor. Initially perceived as facing a cash flow crisis—with negative operating cash flow of RMB 2.2 billion in 2016—Xiaomi rebounded dramatically to generate RMB 12.1 billion in 2017 and RMB 26.3 billion in 2018. This turnaround stemmed from accelerated inventory turnover (4.1x to 6.3x), disciplined capex (R&D held at ~3% of revenue), and a shift to direct online sales, where prepayments covered 65% of Mi.com orders by 2018. Concurrently, Xiaomi leveraged its hardware-plus-ecosystem model to lift blended gross margins from 12.7% to 17.4%, despite smartphone hardware margins remaining modest (4.3% to 8.1%). High-margin internet services surged from RMB 1.9 billion to RMB 15.9 billion in revenue, supported by 190 million monthly active users by Q4 2018. The October 2016 Mi MIX launch elevated average selling prices from RMB 808 to RMB 952, driving a 27% smartphone revenue increase despite flat unit shipments in 2017. Ecosystem synergy was evident as 35% of Mi MIX buyers purchased multiple IoT devices within 90 days, fueling IoT unit sales growth from 20.8 million to 151 million. Working capital efficiency improved markedly—receivables turnover doubled to 9.8x, DSO halved to 37 days, and the cash conversion cycle shortened by 22 days. Critically, all RMB 12.4 billion in preferred stock redemption obligations were settled before the July 2018 IPO, eliminating structural liquidity risk and validating the company’s robust cash-generative model underpinned by 7,584 patents in key technologies. - Word Count : 625]
[Paragraph 4 - Main Point : 【press release：Based on the uploaded financial market data, write...】 - 【第4章：Body Section 1: Comprehensive Financial Performance (2015–2018)】 - Analyze Xiaomi’s 2015–2018 financials using exact metrics from its IPO filing: show how net loss narrowed from RMB -7.6B (2015) to RMB +13.5B (2018); gross margin rose from 4.3% to 12.7%; receivables turnover improved from 5.0x to 7.4x; operating cash flow turned positive at RMB +3.0B in 2017 and RMB +25.1B in 2018; and current ratio recovered from 0.9x (2015) to 1.4x (2018). Explicitly tie each improvement to actions like premium product strategy, supply chain renegotiation, or redemption of RMB 12.7B in convertible preferred shares in 2018. Between 2015 and 2018, Xiaomi executed a comprehensive turnaround that simultaneously strengthened its balance sheet and revitalized operational performance. checklist.name: Financial Analysis Accuracy

checklist.5-6: Accurately presents most financial data but with some minor misinterpretations. Analysis is generally aligned with the provided metrics but lacks depth in connecting data points to form a comprehensive financial narrative.

Near the equator, intense sunlight warms the surface, causing moist air to rise, cool, and release heavy rainfall—fueling rainforests like the Amazon, which receives over 2000 mm of rain annually. This rising air converges at the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ), which migrates seasonally, shifting tropical rains north and south with the sun. As the air moves poleward aloft, it cools and sinks around 30°N and 30°S, creating high-pressure zones of dry, stable air. This subsidence suppresses cloud formation and precipitation, producing Earth’s great subtropical deserts—such as the Sahara, where annual rainfall can dip below 100 mm and temperatures soar to 58°C. The circulation continues through three interconnected cells: the thermally direct Hadley Cell (0°–30°), the indirect Ferrel Cell (30°–60°), and the polar Hadley-like Polar Cell (60°–90°). Together, these act as Earth’s 'air conveyor belts,' redistributing heat and moisture and anchoring climate patterns firmly to latitude—not arbitrary labels. As air rises over mountains, it expands and cools at an average environmental lapse rate of 0.6°C per 100 meters of elevation gain. This cooling reduces the air’s capacity to hold moisture, often triggering orographic rainfall on windward slopes. Consequently, highland regions like the Andes exhibit markedly cooler climates than surrounding lowlands—even near the equator—supporting unique ecosystems such as páramo grasslands. On the leeward side, however, the now-dry air descends, warms adiabatically, and creates a 'rain shadow' effect. This phenomenon leaves areas like eastern Patagonia in Argentina strikingly arid despite their proximity to moisture sources, receiving far less precipitation than expected for their latitude. Rain shadows thus override the general circulation pattern, turning what might otherwise be temperate or humid zones into deserts. checklist.name: Conversational Transformation
checklist.criteria_description: Evaluates how effectively the technical product manual information is transformed into a conversational, engaging script suitable for a livestream format, with appropriate tone, pacing, and interactive elements.
checklist.1-2: Manual information is directly copied with minimal transformation; reads like a technical document with no conversational elements or livestream-appropriate language.
checklist.3-4: Basic attempt at conversational tone but still heavily formal and technical; lacks natural flow and interactive elements needed for livestream engagement.
checklist.5-6: Adequate transformation of technical content into more conversational language, though some sections remain too formal or technical for the target audience.
checklist.7-8: Strong conversational tone throughout with good pacing and interactive elements; script flows naturally and engages viewers while conveying product information.
checklist.9-10: Exceptional transformation that perfectly balances product information with engaging, conversational language; includes natural transitions, rhetorical questions, and audience engagement techniques that make technical information accessible and interesting.

checklist.name: Audience Appropriateness
checklist.criteria_description: Assesses how well the script is tailored specifically for women aged 25-35, including language choices, relatable examples, and empathetic expressions that resonate with this demographic.
checklist.1-2: No consideration of target audience; language and examples are generic or inappropriate for women aged 25-35.
checklist.3-4: Minimal audience targeting; occasionally uses language that might appeal to target demographic but lacks consistent relevance and empathy.
checklist.5-6: Adequate targeting with some relatable language and examples for women 25-35, though lacking depth in understanding their specific skincare concerns and lifestyle.
checklist.7-8: Strong audience focus with language, examples and empathetic expressions that clearly resonate with women 25-35; demonstrates good understanding of their skincare priorities.
checklist.9-10: Exceptional audience targeting that demonstrates deep understanding of 25-35 year old women's skincare concerns, lifestyle, and communication preferences; creates genuine connection through perfectly calibrated language, highly relatable examples, and authentic empathetic expressions.

checklist.name: Technical Accuracy & Simplification
checklist.criteria_description: Evaluates how accurately the script presents the product's technical information while simplifying it into everyday language without exaggeration or misrepresentation.
checklist.1-2: Significant technical inaccuracies or gross exaggeration of benefits; completely misrepresents the product or oversimplifies to the point of being misleading.
checklist.3-4: Contains several technical inaccuracies or exaggerations; attempts at simplification often result in incorrect information or misleading claims.
checklist.5-6: Generally accurate with occasional minor inaccuracies; simplifies technical concepts adequately but sometimes oversimplifies or uses unclear analogies.
checklist.7-8: Technically accurate with good simplification of complex concepts; uses clear everyday language and appropriate analogies without exaggerating benefits.
checklist.9-10: Perfectly accurate representation of all technical information with exceptional simplification into accessible everyday language; uses brilliant, intuitive explanations and analogies that maintain complete factual integrity while making complex skincare science easily understandable.

checklist.name: Script Structure & Timing
checklist.criteria_description: Assesses how well the script is structured for a 3-5 minute presentation, including appropriate pacing, logical flow, clear sections, and efficient use of time.
checklist.1-2: No discernible structure or consideration of timing; would be impossible to present within 3-5 minutes or has major organizational flaws.
checklist.3-4: Poorly structured with timing issues; lacks clear sections or logical progression, likely running significantly over or under the 3-5 minute timeframe.
checklist.5-6: Basic structure with recognizable beginning, middle and end; would roughly fit within 3-5 minutes but has pacing issues in some sections.
checklist.7-8: Well-structured script with good pacing, logical progression between topics, and efficient use of time; clearly designed to fit the 3-5 minute timeframe.
checklist.9-10: Expertly structured script with perfect pacing for livestream delivery; includes precisely timed sections, seamless transitions, strategic emphasis on key selling points, and ideal balance of information and engagement to maximize the 3-5 minute timeframe.

checklist.3-4: Incorporates only basic product information with significant omissions; fails to integrate pricing, user feedback or other important elements from the materials.

checklist.9-10: Masterful integration of all critical information from the materials, perfectly balancing product benefits, usage instructions, pricing, and authentic user feedback within a completely cohesive narrative; prioritizes information strategically while ensuring nothing important is omitted.

checklist.name: Specificity_and_Actionability
checklist.criteria_description: Evaluates the precision, detail, and practical applicability of the recommendations provided in the content optimization plan, including concrete examples, specific techniques, and implementable strategies.
checklist.1-2: Recommendations are extremely vague and generic; lacks any specific examples or actionable guidance; provides no concrete techniques that could be implemented; fails to include the required 5 viral title examples.
checklist.3-4: Recommendations lack sufficient detail for implementation; provides some examples but they're underdeveloped; viral title examples are present but generic; guidance on paragraphs, length, and interactivity lacks specificity and concrete steps.
checklist.5-6: Recommendations include a moderate level of detail; provides the required 5 viral title examples though some may lack creativity; offers general guidelines for paragraphs, length, and interactivity that could be implemented with additional development.
checklist.7-8: Recommendations are specific and practical; provides 5+ thoughtful viral title examples with clear strategic rationale; includes detailed techniques for crafting eye-catching paragraphs; gives specific word count ranges and section proportions; offers concrete interactivity suggestions.
checklist.9-10: Recommendations are exceptionally detailed, innovative and immediately implementable; provides 5+ brilliant viral title examples with strategic analysis for each; includes sophisticated paragraph-crafting techniques with examples; presents precise word count recommendations with optimal section proportions backed by platform insights; offers creative and highly specific interactivity strategies with implementation steps.

checklist.name: Technical_Understanding_of_Content_Engagement
checklist.criteria_description: Assesses the response's demonstration of sophisticated knowledge about content optimization principles, audience psychology, platform algorithms, and engagement metrics that influence content performance in self-media contexts.
checklist.1-2: Shows fundamental misunderstanding of content engagement principles; recommendations contradict established best practices; demonstrates no awareness of how platforms promote content or how audiences engage with it.
checklist.3-4: Demonstrates only surface-level understanding of content engagement; recommendations rely on obvious tactics without deeper strategic insights; shows limited awareness of platform algorithms or audience psychology factors.
checklist.5-6: Demonstrates adequate understanding of basic content engagement principles; recommendations align with conventional best practices; shows some awareness of how platform features influence content performance but lacks sophisticated insights.
checklist.7-8: Demonstrates strong understanding of content engagement mechanics; recommendations incorporate insights about audience psychology and platform algorithms; shows clear awareness of how different optimization strategies affect various engagement metrics.
checklist.9-10: Demonstrates exceptional mastery of content engagement principles with nuanced insights; recommendations reveal sophisticated understanding of platform-specific algorithms, audience behavior patterns, and psychological triggers; expertly explains how each optimization strategy targets specific engagement metrics with anticipated outcomes.

checklist.name: Adaptability_to_Self-Media_Context
checklist.criteria_description: Evaluates how well the content optimization plan addresses the specific challenges and opportunities of self-media publishing across different platforms, demonstrating awareness of the unique characteristics of creator-driven content.
checklist.1-2: Shows no understanding of self-media context; recommendations could apply to any content format; fails to address the unique position of individual creators versus institutional publishers; ignores platform-specific considerations entirely.
checklist.3-4: Shows limited understanding of self-media context; recommendations insufficiently differentiate between platform approaches; minimal consideration of how individual creators can leverage their unique voice or position; lacks platform-specific adaptation strategies.
checklist.5-6: Shows basic understanding of self-media context; recommendations acknowledge some differences between platforms; includes some consideration of creator authenticity and voice; provides general adaptation strategies that would require further refinement.
checklist.7-8: Shows strong understanding of self-media context; recommendations are clearly tailored to self-media creators; includes thoughtful consideration of creator positioning and authentic voice; provides specific platform adaptation strategies based on case study insights.
checklist.9-10: Shows exceptional understanding of self-media ecosystems; recommendations demonstrate sophisticated awareness of creator-specific advantages and challenges; provides brilliantly crafted strategies that leverage creator authenticity while optimizing for platform mechanics; includes advanced adaptation techniques that would give creators competitive advantages across different contexts.
